findings.fact: StartPlayerDialogRemote does not read its input argument in the pinned server binary.
findings.evidence: InputStartPlayerDialogRemote 0x1029f060 performs the shared guards, FinishTalking and virtual setup, writes the forced byte at NPC+0x6495, and schedules code 0x6e without loading the input variant.
findings.consequence: The authored Remote 256 value cannot select placement, first person, or a decoded flag in this handler; the port must not assign it inferred bit semantics.

findings.fact: The ordinary, remote, and unforced openers are non-identical handlers.
findings.evidence: 0x1029ef80 and 0x1029f120 store an integer at NPC+0x5bac and schedule 0x6d; 0x1029f060 does not store it and schedules 0x6e; unforced alone applies the player refusal predicate and clears NPC+0x6495.
findings.consequence: The three Tier-1 bindings require separate handlers and diagnostics even where they share later conversation primitives.

findings.fact: No opener handler writes a player or NPC transform, velocity, camera pose, or input mode.
findings.evidence: The complete bodies at 0x1029ef80, 0x1029f060 and 0x1029f120 contain guards, dialogue cleanup/setup, two NPC state writes, and schedule selection only.
findings.consequence: Physical placement/facing cannot be implemented from the opener inputs; it remains gated on downstream static evidence or the hash-gated capture recipe.
